mainTopic: הנח לישראל, loans on שבת and יום טוב (רבית, court claims, שמיטה, collateral), consecrating a פסח on שבת, and a new משנה on counting and drawing lots
overview: This amud opens by finishing an explanation of why women may draw water on יום טוב in the normal way, since every change would lead to a worse problem. רבא בר רב חנן asks why nobody stops people from clapping and dancing on יום טוב. אביי answers with the principle הנח לישראל: it is better that people sin without knowing than on purpose. The גמרא proves from תוספת יום הכפורים that this applies even to Torah laws. Next, the גמרא settles our משנה about borrowing loaves with הלל's concern about רבית: it depends on whether bread has a fixed price. רב יוסף and רבה argue whether a loan made on יום טוב can be claimed in court, and the גמרא tests this against the cloak rule and a משנה about meat sold on ראש השנה after שמיטה. The גמרא then discusses רבי יוחנן's rule that one may consecrate a פסח on שבת and a חגיגה on יום טוב, and concludes that this applies only to offerings with a fixed time. The amud ends with a new משנה about counting guests from memory and drawing lots at the table and for קדשים.

steps.title: No practical way to change how water is drawn
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes explaining why women may draw water on יום טוב in the usual way: every possible change would lead to a different איסור.
steps.simpleTranslation: Should we make her spread a cloth over the vessel? She might come to squeeze it. Should we make her cover it with a lid? Sometimes the lid's string breaks, and she will come to tie it. Therefore, there is no other way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is closing an explanation of why we do not require women to draw water differently on יום טוב. Each change someone might suggest would cause a new problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A cloth over the vessel could lead to סחיטה, squeezing water out of the cloth. A lid tied to the jug could break and lead to tying a knot, קשירה. Since no safe change exists, women draw water in the normal way.

keyTerms.meaning: squeezing liquid out of cloth, which is forbidden on שבת and יום טוב

phrases.english: Should we spread a cloth [over the vessel]?
phrases.notes: A suggested change to how the water is drawn.

phrases.english: She will come to squeezing [the wet cloth].
Should we cover it with a lid?
Sometimes it gets severed,
and one will come to tie it.
Therefore, it is not possible.
phrases.notes: So women draw water in the usual way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the explanation earlier about drawing water on יום טוב.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical impossibility: every change leads to a different איסור
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We might think women should be required to change how they draw water on יום טוב.
steps.terutzMaskana: Every possible change creates a new risk, so the usual way stays permitted.

steps.title: Why don't we stop people from clapping and dancing on יום טוב?
steps.stepSummary: רבא בר רב חנן points out to אביי that a משנה forbids clapping and dancing on יום טוב, yet people do it and no one says anything.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא בר רב חנן said to אביי: We learned in a משנה that one may not clap, may not slap one's body, and may not dance on יום טוב. Yet we see people doing it, and we say nothing to them!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא בר רב חנן raises a challenge from real life. The משנה forbids these actions, but in practice people do them and nobody stops them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rabbis forbade clapping and dancing on יום טוב so that people would not come to fix a musical instrument. The question is why the community leaders stay silent when people openly break this rule.

keyTerms.meaning: slapping the hand against the body (for example, the thigh)
and we don't say anything to them

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבָּא בַּר רַב חָנָן לְאַבָּיֵי:
phrases.english: And Rava bar Rav Ḥanan said to Abaye:
We learned: One may not clap, and one may not slap [the body],
and one may not dance on a Festival.
And we see that people do [these things],
and we do not say anything to them!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְקָא חָזֵינַן דְּעָבְדִין, וְלָא אָמְרִינַן לְהוּ וְלָא מִידֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from drawing water to a general question about tolerating common violations on יום טוב.
steps.kashyaTarget: The practice of not rebuking people who clap and dance on יום טוב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the משנה forbids it, the rabbis should be rebuking people. Their silence seems to contradict the law.

steps.title: אביי shows the same problem with sitting at the alley entrance
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers with a counter-question: by your logic, we should also stop the women who sit at the entrance of an alley against רבא's rule, yet we don't.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to your reasoning, what about what רבא said: A person should not sit at the entrance of an alley by the side-post, in case an object rolls away and he comes to bring it back. Yet we see women who bring their jugs and sit at the entrance of the alley, and we say nothing to them!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי does not answer directly yet. He shows that the same puzzle exists in another case, which sets up the general principle he will give next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא forbade sitting at the entrance of a מבוי by the לחי, because an object could roll into רשות הרבים and the person might carry it back. Women sit there anyway and nobody stops them. So the question is not only about dancing; there must be one general reason for staying silent.

keyTerms.meaning: and according to your reasoning (a counter-question)
the side-post marking the edge of an alley (לחי)

phrases.english: And according to your reasoning, [what about] that which Rava said:
A person should not sit at the entrance by the side-post,
lest an object roll away from him
and he come to bring it [back],

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא קָא חָזֵינַן נְשֵׁי דְּמַיְתְיָין חַצְבֵי
phrases.english: and yet we see women who bring jugs
and sit at the entrance of the alley,
and we do not say anything to them!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A counter-question that turns רבא בר רב חנן's question into a general phenomenon.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that silence must mean the activity is permitted
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same silence happens in a case that everyone agrees is forbidden, so silence cannot prove that something is permitted.

steps.title: Leave the Jewish people alone: better unknowing than deliberate
steps.stepSummary: אביי gives the principle: we don't rebuke people who won't listen, because it is better they sin without knowing than sin on purpose.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: Leave the Jewish people alone. It is better that they be unknowing sinners and not deliberate sinners.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי now gives the real answer that explains both cases. We stay silent on purpose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If we rebuke people who will not listen anyway, their unknowing sin (שוגג) becomes a deliberate sin (מזיד). Staying silent keeps their sin at the lighter level. The activity is still forbidden; only the duty to rebuke changes.

keyTerms.meaning: leave the Jewish people alone (don't rebuke them)

steps.whatToRemember: הנח לישראל מוטב שיהו שוגגין ואל יהו מזידין: when people will not listen, we don't rebuke them, so their sin stays unknowing rather than deliberate.
steps.confusionAlert: This does NOT mean clapping, dancing, or sitting by the לחי is permitted. The איסור stays in place; the principle only tells us when not to rebuke.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a major principle in הלכה about when the מצוה of rebuke (תוכחה) applies and when it does not.

phrases.english: Rather: Leave the Jewish people alone;
it is better that they be unwitting [sinners]
and not be intentional [sinners].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the general principle that answers both the question and the counter-question.
steps.terutzResolutionType: General principle explaining why the rabbis stay silent
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Silence suggests the rabbis approve of the activity, or are failing in their duty.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rabbis stay silent on purpose, to keep the sin unknowing rather than deliberate.

steps.title: Some thought the principle applies only to rabbinic laws
steps.stepSummary: Some people concluded that הנח לישראל applies only to איסורים דרבנן, not to איסורים דאורייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: They understood from this that this applies only to rabbinic laws, but for Torah laws, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports how some people limited אביי's principle. This sets up the next step, where the גמרא rejects that limit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both examples so far (dancing and sitting by the לחי) were rabbinic decrees. So some assumed that for a Torah law we must always rebuke, even if people will not listen.

phrases.english: They understood from this
[that] this applies to rabbinic [prohibitions],
but for Torah [prohibitions], no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes a limit on the scope of the principle from step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A proposed reading: הנח לישראל applies only to rabbinic prohibitions.

steps.title: The limit is rejected: the principle covers Torah laws too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects that limit: there is no difference between rabbinic and Torah laws for this principle.
steps.simpleTranslation: But that is not so. There is no difference between rabbinic laws and Torah laws.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the reading from step 5. The proof comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reasoning of הנח לישראל is about the sinner's state of mind, not about how severe the law is. So it applies equally to איסורי דאורייתא.

phrases.english: But it is not so;
there is no difference [whether] with rabbinic [prohibitions]
or with Torah [prohibitions].

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא הִיא, לָא שְׁנָא בִּדְרַבָּנַן וְלָא שְׁנָא בִּדְאוֹרָיְיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly rejects the limit proposed in step 5.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the inference that the principle applies only to rabbinic law
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The two examples happened to be rabbinic, but the reasoning does not depend on that.

steps.title: Proof from adding time to יום הכפורים
steps.stepSummary: Adding time to יום הכפורים is a Torah law, yet people eat and drink until dark and nobody says anything, which proves the principle covers Torah laws.
steps.simpleTranslation: For adding time to יום הכפורים is a Torah law, and we see people eating and drinking until it gets dark, and we say nothing to them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a real-life proof for step 6. Here is a Torah law that people break while the rabbis stay silent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah requires starting the fast a little before nightfall (תוספת יום הכפורים). People still eat right up until dark, and no one rebukes them. That silence over a Torah law shows that הנח לישראל applies to Torah law too.

keyTerms.meaning: addition (extra time added before a holy day begins)
יום הכפורים, the Day of Atonement

steps.whatToRemember: הנח לישראל applies to both rabbinic and Torah laws. The proof is that people eat into תוספת יום הכפורים, a Torah law, and no one rebukes them.

phrases.english: For the addition to Yom Kippur
is from the Torah,
and we see them eating and drinking
until it gets dark,
and we do not say anything to them.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּהָא תּוֹסֶפֶת דְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the proof for the rejection in step 6.
steps.raayaObject: That הנח לישראל applies to Torah prohibitions too
steps.raayaSupportSource: The observed practice of eating into תוספת יום הכפורים without anyone rebuking

steps.title: Quoting the משנה about borrowing loaves
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: a woman may borrow loaves from her friend on שבת, but not using the word for a loan.
steps.simpleTranslation: And similarly, a woman may borrow loaves from her friend.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic by quoting a line from the משנה. This sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The full line of the משנה teaches that on שבת a woman may borrow loaves from her friend but may not phrase it as a formal loan ("הלויני"). The גמרא will examine what this implies about weekdays.

phrases.english: And similarly, a woman [may borrow] loaves from her friend.
phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה. It is understood that she may not use the word for a loan on שבת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic by returning to the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On שבת a woman may borrow loaves from her friend, but not using loan language.

steps.title: Does this imply that a loan of bread is fine on a weekday?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers that only on שבת is loan language forbidden, which would mean a loan of bread is fine on a weekday.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it only on שבת that it is forbidden, but on a weekday it is fine?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws an inference from the משנה: if the problem is only on שבת, then lending bread on a weekday must be allowed. This sets up a contradiction with הלל in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the משנה forbids only loan wording on שבת, it seems to assume that a regular loan of bread is permitted on a weekday. The גמרא will now test that assumption.

phrases.english: Is it on Shabbat that it is forbidden,
but on a weekday it is fine?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּשַׁבָּת הוּא דַּאֲסִיר, אֲבָל בְּחוֹל שַׁפִּיר דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an implication from the משנה just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the משנה permits lending bread as a loan on a weekday

steps.title: The משנה seems to contradict הלל on lending bread
steps.stepSummary: If lending bread is fine on weekdays, the משנה contradicts הלל, who forbids lending a loaf without setting its value because of רבית.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say our משנה does not follow הלל? For we learned: And so הלל would say: A woman may not lend a loaf to her friend until she sets its money value, in case wheat goes up in price and they end up with רבית!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the inference from step 9 by quoting הלל, who forbids lending bread even on a weekday unless its price is set. The next step answers this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If wheat prices rise, returning the same loaf means paying back more value than was borrowed, which is רבית. הלל therefore requires setting a money value at the time of the loan. Our משנה seems to allow a plain loan of bread on weekdays, which would go against הלל.
steps.confusionAlert: The problem is not lending on שבת. Even on a weekday, returning the same loaf after prices rise could count as paying interest.

phrases.english: Shall we say our mishna is not in accordance with Hillel,
for we learned: And so Hillel would say:
A woman may not lend a loaf to her friend
until she sets its monetary value,
lest wheat become more expensive
and they will end up coming to interest!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the inference from step 9 using a teaching of הלל.
steps.kashyaTarget: The implication of the משנה that a loan of bread is permitted on a weekday
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: הלל forbids lending a loaf without setting its value because of רבית, so our משנה would seem to disagree with הלל.

steps.title: The משנה Can Follow הלל: Fixed Price vs. Unfixed Price
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה can match הלל. The משנה is talking about a place where bread has a set price. הלל is talking about a place where it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even if you say the משנה follows הלל, there is no problem. The משנה is talking about a place where the price of bread is fixed. הלל is talking about a place where the price is not fixed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction from step 10. It shows that the משנה and הלל are talking about two different situations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: הלל's worry about רבית exists only when the value of the loaf could change. If everyone knows the set price, a loaf returned for a loaf is no more than what was borrowed, so there is no רבית. Where prices change, returning a loaf later might be worth more, so הלל forbids it.

keyTerms.meaning: Even if you say (the answer works even according to this opinion)
Its price is fixed or set

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the problem with lending food is the risk of prices changing, not the lending itself.

phrases.english: Even if you say it follows Hillel,
this (the Mishnah) is in a place where its price is fixed,
and that (Hillel) is in a place where its price is not fixed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each source deals with a different local situation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to allow lending bread on weekdays even though הלל forbids it.
steps.terutzMaskana: Where the price is fixed, a loan is allowed. Where it is not fixed, הלל forbids it because of רבית.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה on Distrust, and the Dispute About יום טוב Loans
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words 'if he does not trust him.' It then brings a מחלוקת between רב יוסף and רבה about whether a loan made on יום טוב can be claimed in court.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'And if he does not trust him.' It was said about a loan made on יום טוב: רב יוסף said it cannot be claimed in court. רבה said it can be claimed in court.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה. It brings a disagreement between אמוראים that relates to it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees the borrower should pay back. The question is only whether the lender can take him to בית דין to force payment. רב יוסף says no, and רבה says yes.

keyTerms.meaning: It was said (introduces a dispute between אמוראים)
A loan made on יום טוב
It was given to be claimed (it can be collected through court)

steps.confusionAlert: 'Cannot be claimed' does NOT mean the borrower may keep the item. He still has to pay. It only means the lender cannot force him through court.

phrases.english: "And if he does not trust him."
It was said about a loan made on Yom Tov:

phrases.aramaic: רַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר: לֹא נִיתְּנָה לִיתָּבַע,
phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: it cannot be claimed in court,
and Rabba said: it can be claimed in court.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם אֵינוֹ מַאֲמִינוֹ. אִיתְּמַר הַלְווֹאַת יוֹם טוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic based on the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב יוסף: a יום טוב loan cannot be claimed in court. רבה: it can be claimed in court.

steps.title: The Reasons Behind Each Side
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף worries the lender will write the loan down on יום טוב. רבה worries that people will stop lending, and borrowers will lose out on the joy of יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף says it cannot be claimed. If you allow it, the lender will come to write the loan down on יום טוב. רבה says it can be claimed. If you do not allow it, the lender will not lend, and the borrower will end up missing the joy of יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why each אמורא holds his view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף fears that if a court case is possible, the lender will write a record so he can prove the debt later, and writing is forbidden on יום טוב. רבה fears the opposite problem: without legal protection, lenders will refuse, and poor people will not have what they need to enjoy יום טוב. Each side protects a different value.

keyTerms.meaning: He will come to write (a forbidden מלאכה)
He will not give him (will not lend)
The מצוה of rejoicing on יום טוב

steps.whatToRemember: רב יוסף is worried about כתיבה on יום טוב. רבה is worried about losing שמחת יום טוב.

phrases.aramaic: רַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר לֹא נִיתְּנָה לִיתָּבַע:
phrases.english: Rav Yosef said it cannot be claimed:
for if you say it can be claimed,
he will come to write (the loan down on Yom Tov).
Rabba said it can be claimed:
for if you say it cannot be (claimed),
he (the lender) will not give him (a loan),
and he (the borrower) will come to hold back from the joy of Yom Tov.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר לֹא נִיתְּנָה לִיתָּבַע: דְּאִי אָמַרְתָּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning of both opinions given in step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב יוסף's reason is a concern about writing. רבה's reason is a concern about losing שמחת יום טוב.

steps.title: Attempted Proof for רב יוסף from the Cloak Collateral
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says a lender who does not trust the borrower takes his cloak as collateral. That fits רב יוסף, since there is no court option. According to רבה, why not just lend and sue later?
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned: if he does not trust him, he leaves his cloak with him. That makes sense if you say the loan cannot be claimed in court. That is why he leaves his cloak and they settle the account after שבת. But if you say it can be claimed, why leave the cloak? Let him lend it and take him to court!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the משנה's cloak rule to try to prove רב יוסף's view. This also works as a challenge against רבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Collateral is needed when there is no other way to get paid. If the lender could sue in court, as רבה says, the cloak would seem unnecessary. So the משנה seems to assume רב יוסף's view.

keyTerms.meaning: He leaves his cloak with him (as collateral)
Granted, it makes sense (according to one view)
And let him claim it from him (in court)

phrases.english: We learned: if he does not trust him,
he leaves his cloak with him.

phrases.aramaic: אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא לֹא נִיתְּנָה לִיתָּבַע —
phrases.english: Granted, if you say it cannot be claimed,
that is why he leaves his cloak with him
and settles the account with him after Shabbat.
But if you say it can be claimed,
why does he leave his cloak with him?
Let him give it to him and take him to court!

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן אִם אֵינוֹ מַאֲמִינוֹ — מַנִּיחַ טַלִּיתוֹ אֶצְלוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the מחלוקת against the משנה's cloak rule.
steps.raayaObject: רב יוסף's view that a יום טוב loan cannot be claimed in court.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's rule that a lender who does not trust the borrower takes his cloak as collateral.

steps.title: The Lender Just Wants to Avoid Court
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected. Even if suing is possible, the lender may prefer collateral so he never has to go to court.
steps.simpleTranslation: He can say: I do not want to have to stand in judgment before a judge.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof for רב יוסף. Taking a cloak makes sense even according to רבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being allowed to sue does not mean a person wants to sue. Court cases are a burden, so a lender may want collateral to avoid them. The cloak rule therefore fits both views.

phrases.english: He can say: I do not want
to stand in judgment before a judge.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר: לָא בָּעֵינָא דְּלֵיקוּם בְּדִינָא וְדַיָּינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 14.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof is rejected. רב יוסף's view is not refuted, just not proven.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed that a lender who can sue would not want collateral. But a lender may want to avoid court altogether.

steps.title: רב אידי בר אבין Begins an Objection: Meat Sold on ראש השנה
steps.stepSummary: רב אידי בר אבין challenges רב יוסף from a משנה. Someone slaughters a cow and divides it among buyers on ראש השנה after שמיטה. If אלול was a full month, שמיטה cancels the debt. If not, it does not cancel.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אידי בר אבין objected: someone slaughters a cow and divides it among buyers on ראש השנה. If the month was made full, שמיטה cancels the debt. If not, it does not cancel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new challenge against רב יוסף. Here it only quotes the source; the actual argument comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sale took place on the day people were keeping as ראש השנה, a יום טוב. If אלול turned out to be full, that day was really still the last day of the שמיטה year, and the משנה says שמיטה cancels the debt. רב אידי בר אבין will argue from this first clause (the רישא): if a יום טוב loan could never be claimed in court, why would the משנה need to say שמיטה cancels it?

keyTerms.meaning: He raises an objection (from a source)
The New Year, first of תשרי

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'full month' means אלול had 30 days, so the first day people kept as ראש השנה was really still the last day of the old שמיטה year.

phrases.english: Rav Idi bar Avin raised an objection:
One who slaughters the cow
and divided it (among buyers) on Rosh Hashana:
if the month (Elul) was full, Shemitah cancels the debt.
And if not, it does not cancel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof for רב יוסף fails, a new source is brought to challenge him.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's ruling that a יום טוב loan cannot be claimed in court.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה says that when אלול was full, שמיטה cancels a debt made on the day kept as ראש השנה. 'Cancels' assumes the debt was claimable, but under רב יוסף a debt made on a day kept as יום טוב is not. The next step states this argument.

steps.title: If the loan could never be claimed, what does 'cancels' add?
steps.stepSummary: רב אידי בר אבין finishes his challenge to רב יוסף. If a יום טוב loan cannot be claimed in court anyway, there is nothing for שמיטה to cancel.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if a loan made on יום טוב cannot be claimed in court, what does the משנה mean when it says שמיטה 'cancels' it?
steps.whatsHappening: This line is the actual attack. It is built on the משנה quoted in step 16. רב אידי בר אבין asks how שמיטה can cancel a debt that was never claimable in the first place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב יוסף, a debt created on יום טוב cannot be collected in court. If so, saying that שמיטה 'cancels' it seems pointless, because the lender could not have sued anyway. The משנה's wording seems to assume the debt was fully claimable, which matches רבה.

keyTerms.meaning: It may be claimed in court
Cancels, meaning the שמיטה year wipes out the debt

phrases.english: And if it cannot be claimed in court
what does 'cancels' mean?
phrases.notes: There would be nothing to cancel.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי לֹא נִיתְּנָה לִיתָּבַע מַאי מְשַׁמֵּט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge whose source was quoted in step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's position that a יום טוב loan cannot be claimed in court.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word 'cancels' assumes a debt that could have been collected. Under רב יוסף, this debt could never have been collected, so the word would have no meaning.

steps.title: In that case the day turned out to be an ordinary weekday
steps.stepSummary: The first case is different. Once אלול turned out to be full, it became clear that the day of the sale was really a weekday, so the debt was claimable.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there, because it became clear that the day was actually a regular weekday.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב יוסף. In the first case of the משנה, the sale did not really happen on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If אלול had 30 days, the day people treated as ראש השנה was really the 30th of אלול. That makes it an ordinary weekday, and also the last day of the שמיטה year. So it was a normal, claimable debt, and שמיטה truly cancels it. רב יוסף's rule about יום טוב loans does not apply to this case at all.

keyTerms.meaning: An ordinary weekday, not a holiday

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the people sinned or that this loan was a real יום טוב loan. Looking back, the day simply turned out to be a weekday, the 30th of אלול.

phrases.english: It is different there
for it became clear that it was a weekday

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאנֵי הָתָם דְּאִיגַּלַּאי מִילְּתָא דְּחוֹל הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: the day was not really יום טוב.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The first case is a יום טוב loan, so 'cancels' would be meaningless under רב יוסף.
steps.terutzMaskana: The first case was really a weekday loan, which is claimable, so שמיטה genuinely cancels it.

steps.title: A new challenge from the second half of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: In the second case the day really was יום טוב. Saying that שמיטה does 'not cancel' the debt only makes sense if it can be claimed, which fits רבה, not רב יוסף.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear from the second half: 'If not, it does not cancel.' If you say a יום טוב loan can be claimed, that explains why it says 'it does not cancel.' But if you say it cannot be claimed, why say 'it does not cancel'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב יוסף again, this time from the second half of the same משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If אלול was not full, the sale really happened on ראש השנה, which is יום טוב. The משנה says שמיטה does not cancel this debt, which implies it is still collectible. Under רב יוסף, though, it was never collectible, so 'does not cancel' seems to give it nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear: an introduction to a proof or challenge
The latter clause of a משנה
It is understandable if you say

phrases.english: Come and hear from the latter clause:
If not, it does not cancel.
It is understandable if you say it can be claimed
that is why it teaches 'it does not cancel.'

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִי אָמְרַתְּ לֹא נִיתְּנָה לִיתָּבַע,
phrases.english: But if you say it cannot be claimed,
why does it say 'it does not cancel'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first half is explained, the גמרא challenges רב יוסף from the second half.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Saying 'does not cancel' implies the debt stays collectible. A debt that could never be claimed would gain nothing from that statement.

steps.title: If the borrower pays on his own, the lender may take it
steps.stepSummary: 'Does not cancel' still matters for רב יוסף. If the borrower pays voluntarily, the lender may accept the money.
steps.simpleTranslation: It matters because if the borrower gives him the money, he may take it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב יוסף by showing a practical result of 'does not cancel,' even when there is no court claim.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if the lender cannot sue, the debt still exists. Since שמיטה did not cancel it, the lender may freely accept repayment when the borrower offers it.

phrases.english: For if he gives it to him, he may take it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing a practical difference beyond going to court.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Does not cancel' only matters if the lender can sue.
steps.terutzMaskana: It matters for voluntary repayment, which the lender may accept.

steps.title: Does that mean that in the first case he may not take the payment?
steps.stepSummary: The answer seems to imply that when שמיטה does cancel a debt, the lender may not accept voluntary payment. That is not true.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this imply that in the first clause, if the borrower gives him the money, he may not take it?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the answer it just gave by pointing out what it seems to imply about the first half of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the difference between the two clauses is 'he may take it,' then in the first clause, where שמיטה cancels, he may not. But a lender may accept repayment of a canceled debt when it is offered voluntarily. So voluntary payment cannot be the difference between the two clauses.

keyTerms.meaning: The first clause of a משנה

phrases.english: This implies that in the first clause
if he gives it to him, he may not take it?!
phrases.notes: Said in surprise. Even a canceled debt may be accepted.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכְּלָל דְּרֵישָׁא אִי יָהֵיב לֵיהּ לָא שָׁקֵיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges what the answer in step 20 implies.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Taking voluntary payment is allowed even after שמיטה, so it cannot be what separates the two clauses.

steps.title: The real difference is whether he must say 'משמט אני'
steps.stepSummary: In the first clause the lender must say 'משמט אני' before accepting payment. In the second clause he does not need to say it.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the first clause, he must say to him, 'I cancel the debt.' In the latter clause, he does not need to say to him, 'I cancel the debt.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sharpens its answer. Both lenders may accept voluntary payment. The difference is whether the lender must first declare that he cancels the debt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a debt canceled by שמיטה, the lender must first say 'משמט אני' before he may accept payment. For a debt that was not canceled, no such statement is needed. So 'does not cancel' still has meaning under רב יוסף.

keyTerms.meaning: I cancel (the debt): the lender's required declaration

steps.whatToRemember: Even under רב יוסף, both clauses of the משנה make sense. A debt canceled by שמיטה needs the declaration 'משמט אני' before payment is accepted. A debt that was not canceled does not need it.

phrases.english: In the first clause, he must say to him
'I cancel the debt,'
in the latter clause, he does not need to say to him
'I cancel the debt.'

steps.triggerLanguage: רֵישָׁא צָרִיךְ לְמֵימַר לֵיהּ מְשַׁמֵּט אֲנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 21 by refining the answer of step 20.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The difference is whether payment may be accepted at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: Payment may be accepted in both cases. The difference is whether the declaration 'משמט אני' is required.

steps.title: Source: a lender must say 'משמט אני' but may then accept payment
steps.stepSummary: A משנה teaches that when a debt is repaid in שביעית, the lender says 'משמט אני.' If the borrower insists, the lender may accept, based on the פסוק 'וזה דבר השמטה.'
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: One who repays a debt in the seventh year, the lender should say to him, 'I cancel the debt.' And if the borrower says to him, 'Even so,' the lender may accept it from him, because it says: 'And this is the matter of the release.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה as the source for the rule it just used: the 'משמט אני' declaration and permission to accept payment afterward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק's words 'דבר השמטה' are read as 'the speech of release.' The lender must verbally cancel the debt, and once he has spoken, he may accept a voluntary payment. This supports the answer in step 22.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה
The seventh year, the שמיטה year
'And this is the matter (or speech) of the release' (דברים 15:2)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical הלכה of שמיטת כספים. The lender says 'משמט אני,' and if the borrower insists on paying anyway, the lender may accept the money.

phrases.english: As we learned in a משנה:
One who repays a debt in the seventh year,
the lender should say to him: 'I cancel the debt.'

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם אָמַר לוֹ ״אַף עַל פִּי כֵן״ —
phrases.english: And if the borrower says to him 'Even so,'
he may accept it from him,
because it says: 'And this is the matter of the release.'
phrases.notes: 'דבר' is read as 'speech': the release is accomplished through words.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the source for the distinction made in step 22.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that a canceled debt requires the declaration 'משמט אני,' after which voluntary payment may be accepted.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in שביעית, based on the פסוק 'וזה דבר השמטה' (דברים 15:2).

steps.title: How two אמוראים handled collateral on a Festival
steps.stepSummary: רב אויא took a משכון for loans given on יום טוב. רבה בר עולא used a clever workaround to get the same protection.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אויא would take collateral. רבה בר עולא would use a clever workaround.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the topic of lending on יום טוב by reporting what two אמוראים actually did in practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This follows the debate over whether a יום טוב loan can be claimed in court. Because the lender might have no court remedy (רב יוסף's view), holding collateral protected him. רב אויא simply took collateral for loans given on יום טוב. רבה בר עולא used a workaround instead: he took something from the borrower after the festival and held it until the loan was repaid.

keyTerms.meaning: Collateral, a pledge taken to secure a loan
Uses a clever trick or workaround

steps.whatToRemember: This closes the lending discussion. Both אמוראים found a way to protect their loans, one directly and one through a workaround.

phrases.english: Rav Avya would take collateral.
Rabba bar Ulla would use a clever workaround.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the discussion of יום טוב loans and collateral with the practical conduct of two אמוראים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Taking collateral for a loan made on יום טוב is a legitimate practice, whether done directly or through a workaround.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: one may consecrate a פסח on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next phrase of the משנה, 'וכן ערב פסח.' It then brings רבי יוחנן's rule that one may be מקדיש his פסח on שבת and his חגיגה on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And similarly, ערב פסח.' רבי יוחנן said: A person may consecrate his פסח on שבת, and his חגיגה on יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line in the משנה and introduces רבי יוחנן's ruling. This sets up the next step, which asks whether the משנה supports him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally one may not be מקדיש things on שבת or יום טוב. רבי יוחנן makes an exception for an offering that is needed for that very day: the פסח on שבת and the חגיגה on יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: The day before פסח, when the קרבן פסח is slaughtered
Consecrates, makes something holy as a קרבן

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a general permission to consecrate on שבת. It covers only offerings that are needed for that day.

phrases.english: "And similarly, the eve of Pesach."
Rabbi Yochanan said:
A person may consecrate his Pesach on Shabbos,
and his Chagigah on Yom Tov.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן עֶרֶב פֶּסַח. אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic based on the next phrase of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person may be מקדיש his פסח on שבת and his חגיגה on יום טוב.

steps.title: Does the משנה support רבי יוחנן?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says that when ערב פסח falls on שבת, a person leaves his cloak with the seller and takes his פסח. This seems to show that an animal can become a פסח on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say the משנה supports him? 'And similarly, ערב פסח in ירושלים that fell on שבת: he leaves his cloak with him, takes his פסח, and settles the account with him after יום טוב.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests that our משנה proves רבי יוחנן's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The buyer gets his animal on שבת and only pays later. So it seems the animal is made into his פסח on שבת itself, which matches רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say this supports him?
Settling the account, making the payment calculation

phrases.english: Shall we say that it supports him?
"And similarly, the eve of Pesach in Jerusalem
that fell on Shabbos:
he leaves his cloak with him,
and takes his Pesach,

phrases.aramaic: וְעוֹשֶׂה עִמּוֹ חֶשְׁבּוֹן לְאַחַר יוֹם טוֹב.
phrases.english: and settles the account with him after Yom Tov."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to support רבי יוחנן's ruling from the משנה.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's ruling that one may be מקדיש a פסח on שבת
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about taking a פסח on a שבת ערב פסח and paying after יום טוב

steps.title: The משנה may be about joining an already-consecrated animal
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected. The משנה may be talking about letting others register on a פסח that was already made holy before שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here, what case are we dealing with? One who registers others with him on his פסח, which was already consecrated from the start.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof by explaining the משנה's case differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the animal was already consecrated before שבת, then nothing is being made holy on שבת. People are only joining a group on it. So the משנה says nothing about רבי יוחנן's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Here, what case are we dealing with?
Registers people as members of a קרבן פסח group

phrases.english: Here, what case are we dealing with?
One who registers others with him on his Pesach,
which was already consecrated from the start.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 26.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof only. רבי יוחנן's ruling itself still stands.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה can be read as a case of registering on an animal that was already holy, so there is no consecration on שבת.

steps.title: But registering on an animal on Yom Tov is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: Another משנה says one may not register on an animal for the first time on יום טוב. Doing so on שבת should be even worse.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned: One may not register on an animal for the first time on יום טוב!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new explanation from step 27 by citing another משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 27 said the משנה is about adding people to an existing פסח. But registering for the first time is forbidden even on יום טוב, and all the more so on שבת. So that explanation seems impossible.

keyTerms.meaning: But we learned in a משנה
One may not register as a member of a group

phrases.english: But we learned:
One may not register on an animal
for the first time on Yom Tov!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the explanation given in step 27.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation that the משנה is about registering others on an already-consecrated פסח
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If first-time registration is forbidden on יום טוב, it should certainly be forbidden on שבת.

steps.title: A regular partner counts as registered from the start
steps.stepSummary: Here the person regularly joins this owner's group. So he is treated as if he had already registered before.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here it is different. Since he regularly joins with him, he is considered like one who was registered on it from the start.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge and saves the explanation from step 27.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban covers only brand-new registration. Someone who always joins this owner's פסח is considered already part of the group. So this is not a first-time registration.

keyTerms.meaning: Is considered like, is treated as

steps.whatToRemember: The proof for רבי יוחנן is rejected. The משנה may be about a regular partner joining an already-holy פסח, and that is not counted as new registration.

phrases.english: Here it is different.
Since he regularly joins with him,
he is considered like one who was registered on it from the start.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 28 and defends the explanation in step 27.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: a regular partner is treated as already registered.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any joining on שבת counts as forbidden first-time registration.
steps.terutzMaskana: A habitual partner is considered registered from the start, so the משנה does not prove רבי יוחנן's ruling.

steps.title: רבי הושעיא's teaching about the shepherd
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says a person may get a lamb from his regular shepherd, make it holy as his פסח, and fulfill his obligation with it. This seems to support רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבי הושעיא taught: A person goes to a shepherd he regularly deals with. The shepherd gives him a lamb for his פסח, and he makes it holy and fulfills his obligation with it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second proof for רבי יוחנן's rule that a person may make his פסח holy on שבת. It quotes a ברייתא in which a person makes a lamb holy for his פסח, apparently on ערב פסח that falls on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier proof from the cloak case (Step 26) was pushed off by saying the animal was already holy before שבת. Here the ברייתא openly says 'ומקדישו', 'and he makes it holy.' That word seems to show the animal is being made holy right now, on שבת itself.

keyTerms.meaning: A Sage who taught ברייתות (teachings from outside the משנה)
And he fulfills his obligation with it

phrases.english: But Rabbi Hoshaya taught:

phrases.aramaic: הוֹלֵךְ אָדָם אֵצֶל רוֹעֶה הָרָגִיל אֶצְלוֹ
phrases.english: A person goes to a shepherd he regularly deals with
phrases.notes: The words 'regularly deals with' will matter for the answer in the next step.

phrases.english: and he gives him a lamb for his Pesach
and he consecrates it and fulfills his obligation with it!
phrases.notes: The key word for the proof is 'ומקדישו', 'he consecrates it.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof was pushed off, this is a new and stronger proof for רבי יוחנן.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's rule that one may make his פסח holy on שבת
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי הושעיא, which says the person makes the lamb holy and fulfills his obligation with it

steps.title: The shepherd already made it holy beforehand
steps.stepSummary: The proof is pushed off. The person regularly buys from this shepherd, so the shepherd made the lamb holy for him before שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: There too, since the person regularly comes to him, the shepherd already made the lamb holy for him from the start, before שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof using the same idea as before. Because this is a regular customer, the shepherd made the lamb holy ahead of time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'הרגיל אצלו', 'whom he regularly deals with', show that the shepherd knew in advance this customer would need a lamb. So the lamb was already holy before שבת, and nothing new was made holy on שבת. This matches the answer in Step 29.

keyTerms.meaning: There too (the same answer works there)
Since he regularly comes to him

phrases.english: There too,
since he regularly comes to him —
he [the shepherd] already consecrated it for him beforehand.
phrases.notes: The bracketed word is a text variant that means the same thing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in Step 30 by reading the case as one where the lamb was already holy.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from רבי הושעיא's ברייתא
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the lamb was first made holy on שבת. In fact the regular shepherd made it holy before שבת.

steps.title: But it says 'he consecrates it'
steps.stepSummary: The answer is challenged. The ברייתא says the person himself makes it holy, which sounds like it happens now.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the ברייתא says 'he consecrates it'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave. The wording of the ברייתא says the buyer is making it holy, not that it was holy already.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the shepherd had already made the lamb holy, why would the ברייתא say 'ומקדישו'? That wording points to a new act of making holy happening right then. This weakens the answer from Step 31.

keyTerms.meaning: It teaches / it says (in the ברייתא)

phrases.english: But it teaches 'he consecrates'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer in Step 31 using the exact wording of the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the lamb was already holy before שבת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא uses an active verb, 'he consecrates', which suggests a new act of making holy and not something done earlier.

steps.title: Only an extra rabbinic holiness
steps.stepSummary: The 'consecrating' in the ברייתא is only an extra, rabbinic-level holiness added on top. It is not the real first act of making the animal holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a 'consecration of addition', and that is only rabbinic.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The owner's 'consecrating' is only an added layer of holiness on an animal the shepherd already made holy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The real הקדש was done by the shepherd before שבת. When the buyer 'consecrates' it now, he only adds extra holiness, called הקדש עילוי, which is just מדרבנן. Such an act may be done on שבת, so the ברייתא is no proof that a real הקדש may be done on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: An added, upgraded holiness on top of holiness that is already there
Only a rabbinic matter, not from the תורה

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the buyer is making a plain animal holy on שבת. The animal was already holy from before שבת. The buyer only adds an extra layer.

phrases.english: It is consecration by addition, which is rabbinic.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording challenge of Step 32 and keeps the rejection from Step 31.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the word 'מקדיש' as a lesser, rabbinic act
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'He consecrates' means the first real act of making the animal holy, done on שבת.
steps.terutzMaskana: It means only an extra, rabbinic-level holiness on an animal that was already holy, so the proof fails.

steps.title: Did רבי יוחנן really say this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן's rule itself. He holds the הלכה follows a סתם משנה, and a סתם משנה forbids making things holy on יום טוב, and even more so on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did רבי יוחנן really say this? But רבי יוחנן said the הלכה follows an unnamed משנה. And we learned in such a משנה: One may not make things holy, make ערכין vows, make חרמים, or separate תרומות and מעשרות. All these were said about יום טוב, and it is a קל וחומר for שבת!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns back to the source of the whole discussion. It asks how רבי יוחנן could allow making a פסח holy on שבת, when he himself rules like a משנה that forbids this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's general rule is that the הלכה follows a סתם משנה, a משנה with no Sage's name in it. Such a משנה says one may not be מקדיש on יום טוב, and שבת is stricter, so it is surely forbidden there. This seems to contradict his rule from Step 25 that one may make a פסח holy on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: Did רבי יוחנן really say this? (a challenge from his own words)
The הלכה follows an unnamed משנה
Making ערכין vows (pledging a person's set value to the Temple)
Making חרמים (dedicating property to the כהנים or the Temple)

phrases.english: And did Rabbi Yochanan say this?
But Rabbi Yochanan said:
The halacha follows an unattributed mishna,
and we learned: One may not consecrate, nor make valuation vows,
nor dedicate property (cherem),
nor separate terumot and tithes,
all of these — they said about a Festival,
all the more so on Shabbat!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן הָכִי? וְהָא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the proofs behind and challenges רבי יוחנן's rule from Step 25 directly.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's rule that one may make his פסח holy on שבת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן follows a סתם משנה, and a סתם משנה forbids being מקדיש on יום טוב, and so all the more on שבת. That is a contradiction in רבי יוחנן's own words.

steps.title: Fixed-time obligations are different
steps.stepSummary: No contradiction. רבי יוחנן allows it for obligations with a fixed time, like פסח and חגיגה. The משנה forbids it for obligations without a fixed time.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. Here, רבי יוחנן speaks about obligations that have a fixed time. There, the משנה speaks about obligations that have no fixed time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the contradiction by splitting the cases. Each source is talking about a different kind of obligation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A פסח or חגיגה must be brought on a set day, so if it is not made holy now, the מצוה is lost. For that reason רבי יוחנן allows it. The משנה's ban covers offerings that can be brought any time, so one can simply wait until after שבת or יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult (the two sources do not clash)
Obligations with a fixed time, such as פסח and חגיגה
Obligations with no fixed time, which can be brought later

steps.whatToRemember: One may be מקדיש on שבת or יום טוב only for an offering tied to a fixed time, like פסח or חגיגה, which would be lost if one waited. For offerings that can wait, the ban in the משנה stays in place.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the general ban on being מקדיש on שבת and יום טוב gives way when the מצוה can only be done at that time.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
here, it refers to obligations that have a fixed time,

phrases.aramaic: כָּאן — בְּחוֹבוֹת שֶׁאֵין קָבוּעַ לָהֶן זְמַן.
phrases.english: there — to obligations that have no fixed time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in Step 34.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן's rule clashes with the סתם משנה that forbids being מקדיש on יום טוב and שבת.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה's ban covers offerings with no fixed time. רבי יוחנן's permission is an exception for fixed-time obligations like פסח and חגיגה.

steps.title: Counting guests and dishes from memory
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: a person may count his guests and his dishes on שבת from memory, but not by reading from a written list.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A person may count his guests and his appetizers from his mouth (from memory), but not from writing.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a new topic. It rules that on שבת one may count guests and dishes out loud from memory, but may not read them from a written list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Counting itself is allowed on שבת when it is done from memory. Reading from a written list is forbidden, and the גמרא will explain the reason later.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה (marks the start of a new משנה)

phrases.english: MISHNA:
A person may count his guests
and his appetizers from his mouth (from memory),
but not from a written list.
phrases.notes: The reason is explained in the גמרא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה with a new topic, separate from the הקדש discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On שבת, counting guests and dishes is allowed from memory but not from a written list.

steps.title: Drawing lots with family at the table
steps.stepSummary: A person may draw lots with his children and household at the table on שבת, as long as the portions are not of different sizes.
steps.simpleTranslation: A person may draw lots with his children and the members of his household at the table, as long as he does not intend to set a big portion against a small portion.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with a second rule. Family members may draw lots on שבת to decide who gets which portion of food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Drawing lots for equal portions is allowed. If the portions are of different sizes, the lottery becomes like gambling, where one person wins at another's expense, so it is forbidden.

phrases.english: A person may draw lots with his children
and with his household members at the table,
as long as he does not intend

phrases.aramaic: לַעֲשׂוֹת מָנָה גְּדוֹלָה כְּנֶגֶד מָנָה קְטַנָּה.
phrases.english: to set a large portion against a small portion.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The second rule of the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Drawing lots at the table on שבת is allowed only when the portions are equal.

steps.title: Drawing lots for holy food on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: On יום טוב one may draw lots for קדשים, but not for the specific portions.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one may cast lots over holy foods on יום טוב, but not over the portions.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends with a third rule. On יום טוב the כהנים may draw lots over קדשים, but not over the separate portions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Drawing lots for קדשים is allowed on יום טוב, but the משנה draws a line at 'מנות', portions. The גמרא will explain exactly what the difference is.
steps.whatToRemember: The new משנה gives three rules: count from memory and not from writing, draw lots at the table only for equal portions, and draw lots over קדשים on יום טוב but not over the portions.

phrases.aramaic: וּמְטִילִין חֲלָשִׁין עַל הַקֳּדָשִׁים בְּיוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.english: And one may cast lots over sanctified foods on a Festival,
but not over the portions.
phrases.notes: The גמרא will explain this distinction.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The third and last rule of the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On יום טוב, lots may be drawn over קדשים, but not over the portions.
